## 5. The original driven pore fails the complete-output comparison

For the potential-switching route, I used a conservative finite-volume calculation with the published triangular geometry and specified reduced parameters:

\[
L_0=5.8,\qquad w=0.65,\qquad
H_c/H_o=18/5,\qquad \gamma=100,
\]

with energies in \(k_BT\) and bare mobility ratio \(\sqrt{20/18}\).

The three comparisons use the same geometry:

1. Independently imposed symmetric switching.
2. Thermal switching with local detailed-balance feedback.
3. The lower barrier held open.

The always-open landscape is the strongest static reference available within this reduced model. Its use does not establish that an equally synthesizable permanently open material exists.

I specified an equal binary feed with total concentration \(2\), a well-mixed receiver at total concentration \(0.2\), and product withdrawal at the receiver composition \(y\). Conservation requires

\[
y=
\frac{K_f(1-0.2y)}
{K_f(1-0.2y)+K_s[1-0.2(1-y)]}.
\]

This prevents a common error: reporting the composition of net transfer as though it were automatically the composition withdrawn from a separately clamped receiver.

### Calculated output at the refined operating point

| Quantity | Always open | Thermal gate | Driven gate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Intrinsic fast/slow permeance ratio | 1.054093 | 1.054018 | 1.120927 |
| Fast-species fraction in withdrawn product | 51.185% | 51.184% | 52.566% |
| Total product rate, relative to open | 1.0000 | 0.5282 | 0.04757 |
| External guest work per product molecule | \(0\) | \(0\) | \(3294.003\,k_BT\) |
| Compositional output rate, relative to open | 1.0000 | 0.5268 | 0.2232 |



::chatgpt-content-reference{index="13"}



The driven gate improves enrichment per molecule, but delivers about **21 times less total product**.

For an ideal mixture at infinitesimal recovery, the reversible compositional free energy per product molecule is

\[
k_BT\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}
\bigl(\mathrm{Bern}(y)\Vert\mathrm{Bern}(1/2)\bigr).
\]

Multiplying that quantity by product rate gives the last row. The driven point produces **4.48 times less compositional output per time and matched geometry**, even before charging its controller.

This is a low-recovery diagnostic, not a complete cascade optimization. Its advantage is that it compares enrichment and throughput together under a balanced collector.

## 6. What the physical ingredients can support

I also made the connection-control construction dimensional, using stable neon isotopes in a conditional gas apparatus.

The example contains sixteen cells with two 1 mL chambers each, 50 μm-radius capillaries of length 30 mm, and gas near 300 K. Knudsen transport supplies the approximate scalar mass dependence; its mass and temperature scaling has experimental support in silicon nanochannels. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"}

For the selected geometry:

| Quantity | Conditional estimate |
|---|---:|
| Neon-20 hopping rate | \(0.004918\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}\) |
| Neon-22 hopping rate | \(0.004689\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}\) |
| Deterministic period | 24.19 minutes |
| Shortest phase | 241.88 seconds |
| Longest capillary diffusion time | 0.0503 seconds |
| Three capillary volumes / one chamber volume | 0.0707% |
| Leading startup relaxation time | About 19.5 hours |

The gross inventory and time-scale requirements can coexist. That is a useful physical consistency check.

The resulting production scale is poor. With total source and receiver pressures of \(1\) and \(0.1\) Pa and a **specified prepared 50:50 neon mixture**, initial stationary transfer is about **1.45 nmol/day**. Five characteristic startup times are roughly four days. A finite receiver’s accumulated composition changes much less than the composition of that tiny newly transferred increment.

Boundary contacts bring the apparatus to 50 channels. Conservative double-ended isolation requires 100 valves and 264 individual state changes per period. Published electrostatic-valve parameters support an approximate capacitive switching scale, but their high-pressure tests do not validate the needed low-pressure leakage, dead volume or absence of valve-induced pumping. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="7"}

The report retains those costs and missing measurements explicitly. It does not combine the 24-minute deterministic apparatus output with the more weakly discriminating stochastic clock’s energy claim.

This could become a demonstrator of ordering control. The matched static comparisons already exclude a separator-efficiency claim at the proposed operating point.

That counterexample protects the theorem’s scope. It does not prove a useful membrane: stronger binding also changes partitioning and can compensate slower self-diffusion in steady permeation. Full transition-state free energies, loading and reservoir coupling remain necessary.

What is established and what should be retained

The retained results are:

A passive comparison law for both long-time diffusion and finite linear permeance under a common equilibrium measure.
A periodic conductance-control law permitting ordering reversal while bounding its magnitude.
An explicit local construction, with exact diffusivity and finite-reservoir output.
A simultaneous finite model containing a noisy clock, nonzero leakage, finite ports and a balanced collector.
A quantitative rejection of the tested efficient-separator proposal
